wa_raven_ridge_standard_route.skip_reason: Approach text stops at the Libby Lake basin, never reaching the gully or ridge: it ends 'A dilapidated cabin sits beside the trail at about 7,170 ft, used by some parties as a base camp.' No climbing is described.

climbing_route.label: Ridge scramble path to the false (south) summit
climbing_route.notes: Past the Snowy Creek Trail #1531 junction the tread thins into more of a ridge scramble path leading to a false (south) summit. No technical climbing when snow-free, but expect loose scree on sections of the switchbacks and essentially no shade or water above the creek crossing.

climbing_route.label: Connecting ridge to the true summit (~6,850 ft)
climbing_route.notes: Use real caution on the short, narrow connecting ridge over to the true summit, which can hold a cornice or residual snow into early summer; genuine route-finding/exposure caution on the false-summit-to-true-summit ridge, especially with snow present. The old lookout foundation and true summit (~6,850 ft) is reached around 3.95-4.0 miles one-way.

wa_ruby_mountain_south_ridge.skip_reason: Approach text stops at the pass, below any climbing: 'continue steeply up the west slopes about 5.2 miles total (2,629 ft gain) to Fourth of July Pass.' Nothing about the South Ridge itself.

climbing_route.label: Lower Ruth Glacier from the toe of the north slope
climbing_route.notes: Rope up and get on glacier gear where the broad ridge feeds the toe of the Ruth Glacier's north slope (~6,000-6,200 ft). The lower glacier is a moderate, welcoming-looking snow/ice slope, but it has produced at least one documented crevasse fall in years with thin or soft cover, so treat it as glaciated terrain the entire way rather than a snow walk.

climbing_route.label: Up and climber's-left to the broad notch northwest of the summit
climbing_route.notes: Continue up and climber's-left to the broad notch just northwest of Ruth's summit (~6,600 ft); most parties camp on the far (south) side of this notch on snow to minimize impact before the final push. No reliable running water above Hannegan Camp/Ruth Creek in a typical snow year.

climbing_route.label: Talus/scree north to the summit
climbing_route.notes: From camp at Eleven Bull Basin, a meadow on Ruth Peak's south flank, scramble class 2-3 talus/scree north to the summit.

wa_scramble_route.skip_reason: Approach text stops at the saddle where the maintained trail ends and only notes that a route exists: 'routes onto Eagle Peak itself continue past the saddle as a scramble.' No description of the scramble is given.

climbing_route.label: Snow basin against the west face
climbing_route.notes: From the Le Conte-Sentinel Col (~7,300 ft), easy scrambling leads onto snow filling the basin against Sentinel's west face; climb increasingly steep snow (can exceed 35-40 degrees, crampons/axe useful) to its top.

climbing_route.label: Ledge leftward (north) across the face
climbing_route.notes: Follow an obvious ledge leftward (north) across the face past a short cliff band.

climbing_route.label: Gravelly/scree terrain to a short step
climbing_route.notes: Turn straight up steep, gravelly/scree terrain to a short step of upper-class-3/low-class-5 climbing.

climbing_route.label: Broad west ridge to the summit
climbing_route.notes: Finish with roughly 600 ft up the broad west ridge to the summit.

wa_sharkfin_tower_southeast_ridge.skip_reason: The text treats the gully as approach ('the tower's obvious approach gully', 'Route-finding here is the crux of the approach') and stops at the base of the climb: 'Follow it up to a notch/terrace at the base of the southeast ridge proper.' The 3-pitch southeast ridge itself is never described.
